newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh may further liberalise business policy.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh may further liberalise business policy.

text.p: Industry and Commerce Minister Tofael Ahmed on Sunday said Bangladesh may further liberalise its trade policy and offer incentives to attract investments.

"We have taken very liberal import and export policies. It is as liberal as you get anywhere in the world and if needed, it would further be liberalised," Ahmed told British business executives at the opening of first ever UK Trade Fair '97.
Ahmed said his government offered "very attractive facilities and privileges to the investors."

He said Bangladesh, where political unrest and poor infrastructure has kept investors away, assured the British businessmen a better atmosphere under the present government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
Ahmed said the government had taken legal and administrative measures to ensure law and order and maintain the "present political stability."
The minister, however, said the level of foreign direct investment had remained very low despite a liberal trade policy.
"Bangladesh has not benefited from increased flow of FDI (foreign direct investment) in the last couple of years," he said.
He said the U.N. Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) had estimated that a "hundred less developed countries received only 1.0 percent of the total FDI flow."
"Such a situation you will aprreciate cannot continue for long," he said.
Ahmed invited British investors to set up a separate industrial zone of their own as Bangladesh had allowd South Koreans to establish recently.

"The South Koreans are expected to commence work on their proposed EPZ (export processing zone) in April," he said. British Cairn Energy Plc signed a new $150 million investment in Bangladesh's state-owned Petrobangla. Cairn has already found huge gas reserves in the Bay of Bengal.

Britain's Commonwealth Development Cooperation (CDC) recently signed a contract with the Bangladesh government to open its office to extend its investment portfolio, which at the moment is around 50 million sterling.
